answer.origin: Fox News Digital feature by Amanda Macias dated 2026-07-01, quoting Corning Chairman, CEO and President Wendell Weeks (party statement) and Emily Capek, Corning planning supervisor. The NVIDIA-Corning facility and jobs claims and the Wistron claim are Fox News reporting with no primary source in the record.
answer.note: The source is a Corning-focused feature, not an NVIDIA disclosure. Its material NVDA-relevant claim is that NVIDIA partnered with Corning earlier in 2026 to build three advanced optical manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas, expected to create more than 3,000 jobs and to expand Corning's US optical manufacturing capacity tenfold (Fox reporting, 2026-07-01, no completion date). Weeks separately said Corning would probably double in size over the coming years, with almost all new hires in advanced manufacturing, a significant part in the US; this is a forward company forecast with no year or baseline. Fox also reports that Taiwan-based Wistron is establishing AI supercomputer manufacturing operations in Texas for NVIDIA, with no job count or date. Conditional interpretation: if these reports are accurate, NVIDIA's AI networking and system supply chain is extending into new US optical and assembly capacity, which supports a read of expanding US-based supply for NVIDIA-linked AI infrastructure. The source does not show NVIDIA's own commitments, purchase volumes, revenue, or margin effect, so it supports a supply-side and ecosystem lead, not a quantified demand or earnings conclusion for NVDA.
limitations: The source gives no NVIDIA-side statement on the Corning partnership: the commercial form (purchase commitment, offtake, co-investment, or joint venture) and NVIDIA's financial obligation are undescribed.
No completion or ramp date is given for the three Corning-NVIDIA facilities, so timing of any capacity effect is unknown.
The tenfold US optical capacity expansion and the 3,000-job figure are Fox reporting with no primary Corning or NVIDIA document in the record; their basis is unverified.
Weeks's double-in-size statement has no stated year, baseline, or measure, so it cannot be converted into a Corning revenue or volume figure.

The Wistron Texas operations have no disclosed scale, investment amount, job count, or start date, and the source does not state the contract terms between Wistron and NVIDIA beyond the phrase for NVIDIA.
The record contains no NVDA filing, earnings figure, or price-relevant data, so the note cannot assess materiality to NVIDIA's results.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA press releases, 8-K filings, and annual report disclosures for the Corning partnership: terms, any purchase or offtake commitment, capital contribution, and stated facility timelines.

Check Corning's press releases and filings for the North Carolina and Texas optical facility announcements, including capacity figures, completion dates, and whether NVIDIA is named as customer or partner.
Check Wistron announcements and Taiwan exchange filings for the Texas AI supercomputer facility: investment size, headcount, start date, and whether the work is for NVIDIA-designed systems.
Check whether any later Corning or NVIDIA statement quantifies the tenfold capacity figure or the 3,000-job estimate, and whether it changes the scope or timing.
